ce983f020d172d953853229ad8f99a275dd78b74.ramble: create a market scanner which scans markets and products of interest to a capybara.
ce983f020d172d953853229ad8f99a275dd78b74.summary:
The app is built. Since the directory was empty, I created a single self-contained `index.html` — the BaraMarket Capybara Market Scanner — which covers all four plan items:

- **Capybara product categories**: six interest categories are defined (Food & Forage, Habitat & Shelter, Aquatic & Swimming, Enrichment & Play, Grooming & Wellness, Social & Companionship), each with weighted relevance keywords, plus anti-keywords (cages, predators, electronics) that penalize a listing's score.
- **Scanner**: pressing START SCAN runs an animated async crawl over seven built-in market feeds (Pantanal Wholesale Exchange, Izu Onsen Supply Co., Rodent Republic Online, etc. — 35 listings total), with a live console log, progress bar, and running stats for markets scanned, listings crawled, and matches found.
- **Relevance filtering**: each listing gets a 0–100% capy score from the keyword engine; a configurable threshold (30/50/70/90%) decides what counts as a match, and after the scan you can further filter by category chips or free-text search (e.g. "melon", "pool").
- **Display & export**: matches render as per-market cards with product tables showing category, price, score pill, and the keywords that matched; the current filtered view can be downloaded as JSON or CSV.

Opening `index.html` in a browser is all that's needed to preview it — no build step or dependencies.

e14d100e9822d33b45ddf62ddec1f3cafb7b4033.ramble: replace the hardcoded feeds with live client-side fetches from Polymarket's public API (gamma-api.polymarket.com), falling back to the sample data when offline (but clearly label if using offline synthetic data).
e14d100e9822d33b45ddf62ddec1f3cafb7b4033.summary:
The scanner now pulls live Polymarket data instead of hardcoded feeds. Here's what changed in `index.html`:

**Live API integration.** Pressing START SCAN now does a client-side `fetch` to `https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?limit=75&active=true&closed=false&order=volume24hr&ascending=false` (the Gamma API serves CORS-enabled JSON, so this works from a static page). The response is grouped by event tag into up to 8 "feeds" of up to 6 markets each, sorted by 24-hour volume. Each listing carries the market question, resolution description, the YES price in cents (parsed from `outcomePrices`), and 24h volume.

**Graceful fallback.** The scan falls back to bundled fixtures when `navigator.onLine` is false (it skips the network call entirely), or when the fetch fails — timeout after 10 seconds via `AbortController`, non-200 status, empty, or unparseable response. The fixtures (`SAMPLE_EVENTS`) are shaped exactly like the Gamma `/events` payload, so live and offline data flow through the same grouping/scoring/rendering pipeline. `online`/`offline` browser events also log hints to the scanner console.

**Clear synthetic labeling**, in five places: a header badge that reads "⚠ synthetic sample data" (vs. a green "● live · gamma-api.polymarket.com" on success), a red warning banner explaining the data is made up and a rescan retries the live feed, a "⚠ SYNTHETIC" pill on every result card, warn-colored console lines during fallback, and `synthetic`/`data_source` fields in the JSON and CSV exports.

**Scoring adapted to real data.** The old capy keywords (melon, hay, pool) would score every real Polymarket question at 0%, so the interest model was retuned to prediction-market topics while keeping the capybara theme — 🗳️ Herd Politics, 🪙 Capycoin & Crypto, 🏆 Splash Sports, 📈 Forage Economy, 🚀 Curious Snout (Sci & Tech), 🎬 Watering Hole Gossip. Keywords now match on word boundaries (so "ai" doesn't match "rain"), and a small volume bonus rewards busy markets. Category chips, threshold filter, search, and exports all work unchanged against both live and sample data.
